advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an "encrypted" variant to test_startup_fails_closed_on_unusable_authorship_key that creates a bot key with `ssh-keygen -N secret` (mode 0600) and expects "not a usable passphrase-free OpenSSH private key"
evidence: The diff adds `_check_startup_authorship_key` to src/rebar/mcp_server.py. Its docstring says the key must be "loadable without a passphrase by ``ssh-keygen``", and its error text says "not a usable passphrase-free OpenSSH private key (empty, malformed or encrypted)".
The probe runs `["ssh-keygen", "-y", "-P", "", "-f", key_path]`; the empty `-P` is what makes an encrypted key fail instead of prompting.

The test table in the diff lists only ("unset", ...), ("missing", ...), ("directory", ...), ("empty", ...) and ("too-permissive", ...). There is no variant that builds a key with `ssh-keygen -N <passphrase>`.
No other case reaches the passphrase handling: the empty and malformed inputs fail to parse before any passphrase is involved.
advisory.finding: The new authorship-key check promises to reject an encrypted (passphrase-protected) key, but the parametrised test has no encrypted case. So nothing checks that the `-P ""` passphrase handling of the `ssh-keygen` probe fails closed on an encrypted key rather than prompting or passing.
scenarios: A refactor drops `-P ""` from the probe. A passphrase-protected bot key then makes `ssh-keygen` try to prompt at container startup instead of failing with the clear OpcertKeyError, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the parametrised test, add ("encrypted", "not a usable passphrase-free OpenSSH private key"). Under `variant == "encrypted"`, run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f <tmp>/enc-bot -N secret -q`, chmod it to 0600, and set REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY to that path.

dropped.finding: compose_startup_opcert_binding now raises OpcertKeyError whenever REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID is set but REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or identity.signing_key is unset or unusable. Before this change, an MCP server with REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID set and no identity.signing_key returned None and started on the developer-local env/genesis signing path. So configurations that used to start are now rejected (a narrowed accepted input). This applies to any non-box MCP run that exports REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID, which the docs describe as a general principal override. Such a run now aborts startup. There is also no fallback to the default `<tracker>/.opcert-key` and no REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY support, and no migration note covers non-box users.
scenarios: A developer runs `rebar mcp` (stdio) locally with REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID exported for developer-local signing, as documented, without REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY. The server used to start; now it raises OpcertKeyError at startup
An external deployment set REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH but no authorship key. Its MCP server used to start with unbound env-path signing; now it refuses to start
An external deployment followed the previous runbook (REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY = op-cert key, no REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH). It now fails with 'no op-cert key source is set'
